transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't come closer. The last stranger who shouted near this fountain never finished his sentence.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Did others fall into this well, and did any come back?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Some fell. Some stood where you stand and listened too long. Sound carries over the oil, and fear feeds it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What did they bring back, if anything?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Scraps. Mud. Sometimes silence where memory should be. No one returns unchanged.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am Salim, and I am here for my brother Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Lower your voice. Names thin when thrown into this air. I don't know your Omar, and that is safer.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Can you tell me who you are then?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I am Hanash. I have stood at this fountain longer than I can measure. I cannot leave it.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: How long have you been here?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Long enough that counting failed me. Faces faded first, then days, then reasons.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Will you help me find Omar?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I cannot guide you anywhere. I do not know paths, and I cannot step off this stone.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then tell me what I should watch for right here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Watch when the oil tightens before it bubbles. Watch shadows that linger too long. That is when attention shifts.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I came here on a dare that turned wrong, and Omar followed me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Dares die quickly here. Guilt lingers. When fear presses you, will you shout his name or steady it?

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I can keep Omar's name inside if that helps.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: That helps more than shouting ever will.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll pay whatever it costs if it brings him back.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Careful with promises. The king who holds this place notices strong words — they echo here long after you've forgotten saying them.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then stay with me and tell me what travelers did right.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: They stopped chasing answers. They chose one steady thought and held it when the dark tried to pry it loose.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'm scared for Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Fear is honest. But if you let it spill, it feeds the well. I can feel the oil shifting already.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Then help me keep from losing him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Helping you sharpens their notice. I just misplaced a thought while speaking. Still, I will try to slow what I can.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll bear it with you if you show me how.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My jaw is shaking. The houses on one side have gone still. Listen carefully — I cannot give paths, only how to stand without being stripped.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Please, for Omar, give it to me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: The hush has fallen. After I say this, I may forget the moment. Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't repeat it. The square listens for echoes. There is one more — harder to give. My hands won't stop shaking.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am still here.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I won't waste them.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use the first when you feel yourself slipping. Use the second only when the pale hands reach you — not before. The order matters.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Thank you, Hanash.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: You listened when it mattered. Now go before the square closes in further.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I'll remember this for Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Wholeness is not how this place works. But breathing is a start. Don't waste what I gave you.
